answer_text:
Let

\[
I=\int_0^1 (f''(x))^2\,dx.
\]

Using the endpoint conditions,

\[
f(1)=f(0)+\int_0^1 f'(x)\,dx.
\]

Since \(f(0)=f(1)=0\),

\[
\int_0^1 f'(x)\,dx=0.
\]

Now write \(f'\) in terms of \(f''\):

\[
f'(x)=f'(0)+\int_0^x f''(t)\,dt=2+\int_0^x f''(t)\,dt.
\]

Thus

\[
0=\int_0^1 \left(2+\int_0^x f''(t)\,dt\right)dx
=2+\int_0^1 (1-t)f''(t)\,dt.
\]

Therefore \(f\) must satisfy the constraint

\[
\int_0^1 (1-t)f''(t)\,dt=-2.
\]

By Cauchy–Schwarz,

\[
\left(\int_0^1 (1-t)f''(t)\,dt\right)^2
\le
\left(\int_0^1 (1-t)^2\,dt\right)
\left(\int_0^1 (f''(t))^2\,dt\right).
\]

We have

\[
\int_0^1 (1-t)^2\,dt=\frac13,
\]

and the left side is \((-2)^2=4\). Hence

\[
4\le \frac13 I,
\]

so

\[
I\ge 12.
\]

Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz occurs when \(f''(x)\) is proportional to \(1-x\). Let

\[
f''(x)=c(1-x).
\]

Using the constraint,

\[
c\int_0^1 (1-x)^2\,dx=c\cdot \frac13=-2,
\]

so \(c=-6\). Thus

\[
f''(x)=-6(1-x)=6x-6.
\]

Integrating and using \(f'(0)=2\),

\[
f'(x)=3x^2-6x+2,
\]

and using \(f(0)=0\),

\[
f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2x.
\]

This function satisfies \(f(0)=f(1)=0\) and \(f'(0)=2\), and for it,

\[
\int_0^1 (f''(x))^2\,dx
=
\int_0^1 (6x-6)^2\,dx
=
36\int_0^1 (x-1)^2\,dx
=
12.
\]

Therefore the minimum value is

\[
\boxed{12}
\]
